reponse:
Here's what happened (the Nov 12 ingest incident, this past Thursday):

**What broke:** The v2.14.0 deploy at 08:47 UTC (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB, and the ingest-worker pods (512 Mi memory limit) started OOM-looping [3]. Consumer lag exceeded 500,000 messages, with out-of-memory errors in `ingest/worker/batch.go:118` [9]. Result: customer dashboards showed stale data from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC (3h40, SEV2) [1][3].

**Data loss:** No. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late; reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed no event was lost [1]. Maya's customer-facing note to Orbitly says the same [2].

**Changes being made:**
- Revert default `max_batch_bytes` to 1 MB, add a guard refusing batches larger than 25% of the container memory limit; bulk import keeps 10 MB via explicit config on the 2 Gi pool (ingest#419) [6]
- New alert routed to on-call when ingest-events consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes of events (KES-431, due Nov 20) [10]
- Alerts when processing falls more than 5 min behind, and config changes go to a canary group first (per the customer comms) [2]

One follow-up to be aware of: Orbitly is claiming an SLA service credit under section 7 of their MSA; Sam is checking the terms — the signed MSA isn't attached to the HubSpot deal, and it was a custom 2024 negotiation [2][7]. Also note the Postgres 17 cutover planned for Nov 21 was postponed after the incident [5].
